title: Related Rates: Expanding Sphere
caption_md: A balloon inflates at a constant rate $\frac{dV}{dt}=10$ (arbitrary units). The radius $r(t)$ and volume $V(t)=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ are linked, so as the volume grows linearly, the radius grows at a decreasing rate. The blue curve shows $r(t)$; the dashed line shows $V(t)$ (scaled down by $\div 40$ so both fit). The tangent line at $t=3$ shows $\frac{dr}{dt}$ at that instant — notice how its slope is smaller than at earlier times. This is the key idea: even though $\frac{dV}{dt}$ is constant, $\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{dV/dt}{4\pi r^2}$ shrinks as $r$ grows.
